facts.statement: Brontornis lived during the Early to Middle Miocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early-Mid Miocene (Santacrucian-Laventan)~

facts.statement: The first fossils of Brontornis were described by Francisco Moreno and Alcides Mercerat in 1891.
facts.quote: The first fossils of Brontornis burmeisteri were described by paleontologists Francisco Moreno and Alcides Mercerart in 1891

facts.statement: The initial fossils consisted of a left femur, tibiotarsus, fibula, and tarsometatarsus from a single individual found in the Santa Cruz Formation of Santa Cruz Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: the fossils being a left femur, tibiotarsus, fibula, and tarsometatarsus all from the same individual found in the Lower-Middle Miocene strata of the Santa Cruz Formation in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina

facts.statement: Brontornis is an extinct genus of giant birds that lived in Argentina during the Early to Middle Miocene.
facts.quote: Brontornis is an extinct genus of giant bird that inhabited Argentina during the Early to Middle Miocene

facts.statement: The taxonomic position of Brontornis is controversial, with it being alternatively classified as a cariamiform, a phorusrhacid (terror bird), or an anserimorph.
facts.quote: Its taxonomic position is highly controversial, with authors alternatively considering it to be a cariamiform, typically a phorusrhacid (terror bird) or an anserimorph

facts.statement: Cladistic studies have suggested that Brontornis is a basal relative of geese.
facts.quote: After several cladistic studies, the Brontornithidae have been found as basal geese relatives

facts.statement: A 2017 study suggested that Brontornis belongs to the sister taxon of Cariamiformes.
facts.quote: However, a study from 2017 suggested that Brontornis belonged to sister taxon to Cariamiformes

facts.statement: A 2021 study classified Brontornis as a Gastornithiform.
facts.quote: However, a 2021 study once again found Brontornis to be a Gastornithiform

facts.statement: Based on fossil finds, Brontornis is estimated to have reached a height of 280 cm.
facts.quote: Due to the size of the finds, a height of 280 cm is assumed

facts.statement: The massiveness of its bones leads to weight estimates between 319 and 400 kg.
facts.quote: The pronounced massiveness of the bones leads to weight estimates between 350 and 400 kg or 319 to 350 kg

facts.statement: Brontornis is considered the fourth-heaviest bird ever found, after Aepyornis maximus, Dromornis, and Pachystruthio.
facts.quote: These measures would make Brontornis the fourth-heaviest bird found thus far, after Aepyornis maximus, Dromornis, and Pachystruthio

facts.statement: Some fossil finds show size differences of up to 33% based on the tarsometatarsus.
facts.quote: some finds have clear size differences that can reach up to 33% based on the tarsometatarsus

facts.statement: Brontornis is related to seriemas and shares features like a hook-shaped upper beak and curved, sharp claws, indicating it was a predatory carnivore.
facts.quote: These are related to the seriama, sharing features such as a hook-shaped upper beak and the curved ungues, which had sharp claws and thus distinguish the birds as predatory carnivores

facts.statement: The absence of the bone footbridge (Pons Supratendineus) found in Phorusrhacids is a point used to argue against Brontornis being a terror bird.
facts.quote: The lack of the striking bone footbridge (Pons Supratendineus) on the front of the lower joint of the tibiotarsus of Brontornis was also pointed out several times, which in occurs in the Phorusrhacidae

facts.statement: The different design of the lower jaw suggests Brontornis had a different diet than Phorusrhacids.
facts.quote: the different design of the lower jaw also results in a different diet of Brontornis than Phorusrhacids

facts.statement: Brontornis is known from fossils of legs, feet, some skull parts, and vertebrae found in the Santa Cruz province.
facts.quote: Se conoce a partir de huesos, principalmente de las patas y los pies, pero también por algunas piezas de cráneo y columna vertebral, que se encuentra en varias localidades de la provincia de Santa Cruz.

facts.statement: The species B. burmeisteri stood about 2.80 meters tall and weighed an estimated 350-400 kg.
facts.quote: B. burmeisteri fue la especie más grande de su grupo, con una altura de alrededor de 2,80 metros y un peso estimado de 350-400 kg

facts.statement: It is currently the third heaviest bird known after Aepyornis maximus and Dromornis stirtoni.
facts.quote: por lo que es el tercera ave más pesada según los conocimientos actuales (después de Aepyornis maximus y Dromornis stirtoni)

facts.statement: It was the dominant carnivore in Patagonia during the Miocene, capable of killing large animals like the elephant-like mammal Astrapotherium and the predator Thylacosmilus.
facts.quote: Era el carnívoro dominante de la Patagonia durante el Mioceno, siendo capaz de matar incluso a grandes animales como el mamífero similar al elefante Astrapotherium y el depredador Thylacosmilus

facts.statement: Brontornis was an extinct genus of giant flightless birds that lived in Patagonia.
facts.quote: Brontornis es un género extinto de aves no voladoras gigantes que vivían en la Patagonia.

facts.statement: The fossil range of Brontornis spans from the Early Miocene to the Middle Miocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Mioceno inferior - Mioceno medio

facts.statement: The genus Brontornis was described by Moreno & Mercerat in 1891.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Moreno & Mercerat, 1891

facts.statement: It has traditionally been included in the family Phorusrhacidae, or "terror birds," due to its large size and predatory lifestyle.
facts.quote: ha sido tradicionalmente incluida en la familia Phorusrhacidae ("aves del terror") por su gran tamaño y estilo de vida depredadora

facts.statement: Recent studies have questioned whether Brontornis is a phorusrhacid, suggesting instead that it is actually an anseriform.
facts.quote: Algunos estudios recientes han puesto en cuestión la idea de que Brontornis sea un forusrácido; de acuerdo con esta investigación, parece ser realmente un anseriforme.

facts.statement: However, a later analysis interprets Brontornis traits as adaptations for supporting its weight while showing diagnostic thoracic vertebrae of phorusrhacids, reaffirming its membership in that group.
facts.quote: No obstante, un análisis posterior interpreta que los rasgos de Brontornis son adaptaciones para sostener su gran peso, a la vez que exhibe vértebras torácicas diagnósticas de los forusrácidos, reafirmando su pertenencia a este grupo.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest it may have hunted by jumping on prey and knocking it down with attack force after a short chase.
facts.quote: saltando sobre ella y derribándola por la fuerza de ataque después de una corta persecución

facts.statement: Studies on the lower jaw indicate it was likely not suitable for tearing animal food.
facts.quote: Studies on the lower jaw indicate that it was most likely not suitable for tearing animal food.

facts.statement: Some researchers believe Brontornis could have been a carrion eater due to its original placement within the "terror birds" grouping.
facts.quote: Due to the original placement within the "terror birds" grouping, some researchers believe that Brontornis could have been a carrion eater.

facts.statement: Fossils described as B. platyonyx are about one-third smaller than the largest Brontornis bones.
facts.quote: son cerca de un tercio más pequeños que los mayores huesos de Brontornis.
